messages:
maria: Kicking off eu-central-1 region bring-up load/soak now. Plan: 30m ramp to 400 qps, 3h soak at 400 qps, then a 15m peak spike to 700 qps. Focus: GPU pod stability, batcher p95 < 200ms, no KV cache thrashing. Run ID: rg-euc-2026-03-18. @jordan @sam please watch autoscaler + nodepool quotas.

jordan: Ack. Watching cluster-autoscaler events and GPU pool provisioning. Note: initial quota is 24 GPUs in eu-central; if we hit it we should failover to the fallback model (q8 quant). I'll post events.

sam: Running the k6 script from infra/tests/region-launch/k6-euc.js. Command: 
```
k6 run --vus 200 --duration 30m infra/tests/region-launch/k6-euc.js --out influxdb=http://metrics:8086
```
Will ramp to 400 qps by 30m using the ramping scenario.

leo: Quick infra note — the default CA scale-down delay is 10m; for this launch we want scale-down disabled during soak to avoid churn. Jordan, can you set `--scale-down-unneeded-time=0s --scale-down-unready-time=40m`?

jordan: Done. Also changed expander to `least-waste` for GPU pools to prefer filling existing nodes. Applied new CA flags on the controller: `kubectl -n kube-system set args deployment/cluster-autoscaler -- --expander=least-waste --scale-down-unneeded-time=0s`.

maria: Thanks. Two monitoring tasks: 1) watch GPU pod eviction rate and OOM/killed by kubelet, 2) check networking errors to upstream model stores (S3/KV). If either crosses 0.5% error rate we abort.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: rg-euc-launch/2026-03-18T09:00:15Z. Targets: serving-v2 replicaSet v2.14 -> canary subset.

sam: First 30m ramp results: reached 420 qps peak, p50=38ms, p95=185ms, p99=320ms. Noticed transient 503s from nginx-ingress at 20m (about 0.8% of requests) correlated with one GPU node being NotReady for ~90s.

jordan: Looking at node events — GPU driver crashed on node g-euc-07, kubelet restarted, replaced pod, node returned. We saw CA spin up a replacement node. Driver logs attached (snip): 
```
[Err] nvidia: GPU reset required, nv-fan-temp spike, module unload
kubelet: eviction threshold crossed, pod eviction: 1 inference pod
```

leo: Suggestion: increase `gpu-graceful-drain` to 120s and enable daemonset to restart drivers more gracefully. Also raising `pod-disruption-budget` for batchers to 30% to reduce simultaneous disruptions.

maria: Agreed. Make the PDB change now and add a node-level init check for driver health before marking Ready. We can't afford single-node driver restarts to cause 0.5% errors.

jordan: PDB changed to minAvailable=70% for batcher statefulset. Added node readiness probe: `/opt/bin/gpu-driver-health` with 60s initial delay and 15s period.

sam: Running soak at steady 400 qps now. Hour 1: p95 steady ~190ms, p99 down to 290ms after warmup. No additional 503 spikes. GPU utilization avg 78%, memory cushion ~12% per pod.

maria: FYI cost watch: at 400 qps steady we're burning ~180 GPU-hours per day across the cluster, projected extra $12k/week at current reserved pricing if we keep this capacity post-launch. We need a follow-up to tune quantization + batching to reduce per-token GPU time.

leo: Autoscale tuning note: CA was launching mixed instance types which increased variance. Recommendation: pin primary GPU pool to homogenous SKU for first 24h of launch to stabilize. Then can enable mixed types with binpack policy.

jordan: Pinned pool to g4dn.xlarge-ish SKU equivalent for consistency (api applied). Also adjusted HPA for the batcher to use custom metric `inflight_tokens` and set target value to 800. This cuts noisy horizontal autoscaling oscillations.

maria: 3h soak complete. Final spike to 700 qps: sustained 15m. Observed p95=240ms, p99=480ms, error rate 0.9% during spike (mostly 429/503 when CA had small lag). We hit the quota at 24 GPUs and CA queued pods for ~90s while we requested quota increase.

sam: Actions from spike: 1) request quota increase to 48 GPUs in eu-central, 2) implement faster Karpenter-like provisioning for burst (we have a patch to boot from warm pool), 3) add fallback routing to q8-quant models automatically at 80% GPU util.

maria: I'm packaging a region-handoff doc with these items: capacity increase ticket, PDB/GPU-driver probe changes, CA flags, HPA metric config, and cost mitigation tasks (quant + batch tuning). Handing to oncall for next 24h monitor.

leo: Oncall rotation for next 24h: @jordan -> primary, @sam -> infra backup, @maria -> product/launch contact. If errors >1% for 15m, rollback canary and scale down to baseline.

jordan: I'll keep an eye. Posting the summary and the quick commands for rerun/abort in infra/runbooks/rg-euc-2026-03-18.md.

maria: Great work team. We'll do a follow-up session tomorrow to decide permanent autoscale settings and cost tradeoffs. :thumbsup:
